svg.title: OpenRV64 three-pipe core detailed block diagram
svg.desc: Detailed block and connection diagram for the live openrv64_top_3p RTL. It covers the three-wide frontend, dispatch and forwarding fabric, EX0, EX1 and MEM execution pipes, retirement, CSRs and PMP, the MMU, private L1 instruction and data caches, and native 512-bit ICX channels.
svg.text: RTL boundary: openrv64_top_3p · inspected 2026-07-23 10:02 UTC · Git 091bc5ab03b0 + dirty working tree
LIVE RTL DEFAULTS: M=0 · A=1 · BP=STALL · L1I 16 KiB/4-way · L1D 16 KiB/8-way
LAST AREA PROFILE: RV64IM+A · BIMODAL · 8 KiB/4-way L1I + 8 KiB/4-way L1D
INTERNAL DYNAMIC ID = 10 BITS · separate architectural trace UID remains 64 bits
Block sizes are not drawn to physical-area scale.
BACKEND · in-order admission, independent completion, in-order retirement

g.text: Top-level RTL default BP policy is STALL.
system, fence, illegal and fault flags
Cancels fetch slots; optionally keeps stash
FENCE.I invalidates I$; SFENCE.VMA flushes TLBs.
Present in repository, not instantiated here
Scalar RV64F/D module · experimental custom vector unit/cache/LSU
No active FP/SIMD register-file, issue, completion, retirement, or memory connection.
Excluded from the current 3P synthesis source/profile.
Mapped as logic/registers; no RF macro selected.
RV64M is parameterized; physical profile enabled it.
Early aligned branch resolution; held completion.
selective squash by branch slot; no depth-wide count scan
Trace64 is one allocation-only sidebank when enabled.
Area profile disables it; no trace state remains.
retire maximal ordered prefix, up to 3/cycle
GPR writes · CSR writes · branch training
Retirement controls visible architectural side effects.
M/S privilege state · trap CSRs · SATP/Sv39 context
MMU context: priv2, satp mode4, ASID16, root PPN44
Instruction, LSU and PTW protection checks share
Six external IRQ inputs: M/S software, timer, external.
Trace-only counters disabled in physical profile.
Outputs tie to zero when disabled.
No CDC is instantiated inside openrv64_top_3p.

CORE MEMORY SUBSYSTEM · openrv64_core_icx_bus · translated private-cache clients + native ICX

g.text: AXI IDs 0–3 are only used if L1I is disabled.
64 sets · physical tag / virtual page-offset index
miss: one ICX READ size=6 → one 512b beat
Read-allocate; pipelined resident hits; full-line storage.
loads, stores, LR/SC and AMO intent
Same Sv39 entry geometry as I-TLB
stride prefetch: queue4 / up to4 outstanding
load miss: ICX READ line512; refill as 8×64
ICX transaction ID4; core request tag3.
MESI/timestamps are reserved metadata, not coherence.
openrv64_bus_ptw · I-TLB / D-TLB / speculative I$ xlate
3-level walk · one active walk state machine
extracts selected PTE from a 512-bit ICX line
Not mapped to an SRAM macro in current flow.
kind = PTE · cacheable · ordered identity check
ICX cmd: READ, size=6, addr64, burst=0
SFENCE aborts or invalidates in-flight state.
PTW traffic is native ICX; it does not use AXI.
Native ICX client arbiter / response demux
three clients: L1I source0 · L1D source1 · PTW source2
held-grant command arbitration with source/txn routing
independent command, write-data and response channels
hart4 txn4 source2 op4 lock1 order2
L1D is the only active write-data producer.
Responses are accepted only by matching source/txn.
This is a native cache-facing transport, not AXI.
It carries LR/SC/AMO intent, but the present private
L1 metadata does not implement a coherent protocol.
No probe/snoop/ack channel exists at this boundary.
single clock domain; external fabric supplies backpressure
Carries all enabled L1I, L1D and PTW traffic.
External cache/L2/fabric is outside this diagram.
Used only when L1I is explicitly disabled.
No scalar LSU or PTW request uses this path.
With enabled caches, AXI outputs optimize to tie-offs.
Legacy generic 64-bit blocking bus is also tied off.

svg.text: The live RTL defaults shown above are 16 KiB 4-way L1I and 16 KiB 8-way L1D.
The last corrected physical-size run used 8 KiB 4-way caches and inferred 4 × 32×512 L1I plus 4 × 256×64 L1D RAMs.
Its 4.202 mm² standard-cell total and 16 KiB aggregate SRAM therefore do not describe the current wrapper defaults without a rerun.
Internal dynamic IDs are 10 bits; the independent 64-bit trace UID remains embedded in issue and completion payloads.
Sources: rtl/openrv64_top_3p.v, rtl/core/rv64_top_3p.v, rtl/core/backend/backend_3p.v, rtl/core/bus/icx_bus.v, rtl/core/cache/l1/l1i/l1i.v, rtl/core/cache/l1/l1d/l1d.v.
ready/valid handshakes are stated in labels; reverse ready wires are not drawn separately.
